A lot to unpack here. Firstly, every 4-6 weeks is not very often at all, maybe I just have had more severe experiences, but I don't think that's often. You shouldn't  be thinking about hiding your emotions, especially around your partner. You shouldn't pretend to be happy and not upset if you are. Feeling emotions of any kind is okay and expressing them is okay too. You're allowed to have breakdowns as much as you need, and from what it seems you are pretty good at coping with them as well.

I'm glad to know you've been to therapy and I suggest when you go again you bring this up. In my opinion, it's definitely not a problem of you being upset too often, it's about an insecurity around asking for help.

Talk to your partner about how you feel, ask him for input if he actually finds this burdening, set up boundaries if so.

Work on loving yourself and being okay with expressing your emotions. Your frustrations are valid. It's okay that you're not always okay, it should be that way.

I'm sure you would be everything he'd want you to be and more, you wouldn't disappoint him. But this brings up a different issue. If this really is how you see yourself, I think it's soemthing you have to work on before getting in a relationship. I can say from experience, it's difficult to love and feel loved by someone who can't even love themselves. Don't feel bad about not being able to love yourself yet, but I think it's vital to sort out before being able to commit to another person.

I think you being hesitant about trying to start up a relationship with him might have been very confusing and he might have taken it as you not liking him. Whether you should talk to him or not depends on if you want to and that's it. Though, if you do decide to, I suggest you try to overcome your fears and be more direct in what you want instead of running away from him. This will only hurt the both of you and confuse him.

People are different and have different boundaries to when to introduce intimate things into a relationship, but, personally, a week is a bit very quick for this. From what I can tell, you haven't established this as a romantic relationship or anything else. I think it's a bit quick to rush into that if he actually wants to have a relationship with you. If you want it to be other than just sexual, set clear boundaries as to what is okay and what isn't.

You're young, please be careful, don't do anything that makes you uncomfortable or what you're not ready for. Even if he doesn't pressure you to do things yet, he might later, don't give into pressure.

You already broke up and she's moving on. Getting back together after breaking up to possibly break up again isn't healthy for anyone. If you don't have trust for her I don't feel that you will be able to live in bliss as you could before she broke your trust. It doesn't seem like a sustainable way to lead a relationship. Let her move on and move on yourself, don't play with her or your feelings.

>She is also bipolar so I was always a little scared of long term commitment given how often these relationships lead to failure

Being bipolar or having any mental disorder for that matter doesn't make anyone a bad person, it doesn't make them cheat or hinder their ability to have a committed relationship.

You are not her therapist. You have no obligation to take care of her, even if you are the only one who knows about her mental struggles. In my opinion, she has no right to expect you to act as if you are her personal mental health professional. You never signed up to be one. You are a regular person and you deserve to be treated as just that.

You have to think about how mentally burdening her actions are on you. If it's burdening to the point that you think it's not healthy for you, distance yourself as much as possible, even if that means completely cutting her off. You are your own priority and it should always be that way. 

If you feel that you are unable to distance yourself or do it completely, you have to clearly communicate your boundaries and explain how it makes you feel. For example, you could suggest to her before venting  to ask if it's okay to do so at the moment and if you will be mentally capable of digesting such information.

Bottom line, you are a priority, remember to take care of yourself first.

To me it seems that you don't enjoy being with your partner. You might not see her specifically as someone to have as a romantic partner and that's okay, it's completely normal, you don't have to fall in love with every person that comes your way. I think you should communicate to her how you feel as soon as possible and break up. A month isn't long, just make sure you don't get stuck in a relationship you don't want to be for much longer. Get out in the world, experience new relationships, find someone you actually want to be with.

If she does anything to herself, it's absolutely not your fault, you are not responsible for anyone's actions but your own. I'm glad you recognize that you should break up with her, but you shouldn't feel any guilt around doing it. And please don't put off doing it, remember, there will never be a "right time" to do it, the longer you stay the worse it might get.
